title: service-discovery-federation-and-gpu-telemetry-strategy
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a lightweight, pragmatic architecture for a federated service discovery and cluster inventory system focused on GPU-aware routing decisions across multiple regions. Primary goals: make routing decisions reliable and debuggable, expose a concise node schema for match/ranking, and emit health/telemetry signals that let the control plane detect degradation before customer impact.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Dedicated and Private control planes; hosted API will consume same query API but may use a thin global caching layer.
- We assume each region operates an authoritative local registry (region-local control plane) and there is a global federation layer for cross-region queries.
- Metrics and events flow via OpenTelemetry-compatible exporters; control plane stores lightweight aggregated state in a resilient datastore (e.g., CockroachDB or regional etcd clusters).
- Node-level agent runs on every node and reports labels, capacity, and health probes.

Quick summary of design choices (TL;DR):
- Node schema: compact key/value labels with normalization and a small fixed set of enumerations for GPU family, power class, and node_role.
- Health model: heartbeat + orthogonal probes (GPU driver, NVML, disk, network) with simple aggregated health score (0-100).
- Federation: Eventually-consistent regional registries, change-log replication to global index for read-heavy cross-region routing.
- Routing API: returns scored candidates (score vector + metadata) instead of a single decision; client or router applies policy weights.

1) Node registry / inventory schema (single-line examples, aim for stable keys)
- node_id: uuid (redwood-node-xxxx)
- region: e.g. us-west1, eu-central1
- zone: optional, e.g. us-west1-b
- node_role: serving|batch|infra|gpu-pool (enum)
- gpu_vendor: nvidia|amd|intel (enum)
- gpu_model: normalized string, e.g. a100-40gb, h100-80gb, mi250x
- gpu_compute_tier: genX-large|genX-medium|genX-small (semantic tier for scheduling)
- gpu_mem_gb: integer (round to nearest 4GB)
- cpu_cores: integer
- memory_gb: integer
- local_ssd_gb: integer
- max_concurrent_requests: integer (capacity units, CU)
- labels: free-form short k/v for customer tags (max 16 entries)
- last_heartbeat_ts: RFC3339
- health_score: integer 0-100

Label normalization rules (important to keep consistent queries):
- gpu_model must be lowercase, hyphen-separated, vendor prefix optional (normalize to vendor_model where ambiguous).
- gpu_mem_gb is numeric bucket (16, 24, 40, 80, 96).
- node_role enumerations are intentionally small; encourage teams to use labels[] for team-specific attributes.
- Disallow long free-text in gpu_model; prefer canonical entries maintained in a small central catalog.

2) Health signals and probes (agent -> control plane):
- Heartbeat: agent pings every 20s with a small delta payload (node_id, ts, incremental sequence). If 3 heartbeats missed -> mark stale.
- GPU liveness: NVML probe for driver alive + per-GPU health flags (ECC errors, Xid codes). Report as boolean + last_error_code.
- GPU utilization: moving average of GPU util % (1m, 5m) and free_mem_mb.
- Memory pressure: swap_used_pct, mem_available_mb.
- Disk: disk_util_pct and IO wait (avg 1m).
- Network: egress latency to regional gateway (p95) and packet loss rate.
- Kernel / OOM events: stream last N entries, increment error counters.
- Custom readiness gates: e.g., model cache warmed flag (optional for serving nodes).

Health scoring (simple, defensible):
- Base 100, subtract weighted deltas: 20 pts for missing heartbeat, 30 pts for NVML fatal errors, up to 20 pts for sustained gpu_util>98% and 10 pts for disk_io_bound, 10 pts for network anomalies.
- health_score < 40 -> node considered UNHEALTHY for routing; 40-70 -> degraded (lower weight), >70 -> healthy.

3) Registration/Agent behavior and data plane contract:
- Agent registers node on boot and pushes full label+capacity snapshot every 5 minutes. Heartbeat every 20s.
- Agent exposes a local admin HTTP endpoint for introspection (node metadata, last probes, raw NVML logs) for SRE debug access.
- When a node's gpu_model or capacity changes (e.g., driver upgrade, instance resize), agent annotates event with versioned delta (old->new) and control plane runs a lightweight reconciliation.

4) Regional registry and federation model:
- Each region has an authoritative registry service (region-registry) that owns the canonical state for nodes in that region.
- A change-log (append-only mutations) is produced per region; a global federation index consumes region logs and maintains a searchable cross-region index optimized for read-heavy queries (time-decayed materialized view).
- Use monotonic sequence numbers per region to simplify reconciliation and allow idempotent replay. Avoid synchronous cross-region writes for node updates (latency-sensitive).

Replication / consistency guarantees:
- Local read-after-write: within a region, clients reading node data get strong-ish consistency (we accept small window for eventual convergence on failover).
- Cross-region queries: eventual consistency with TTL-based staleness tolerated (configurable, default 60s for routing decisions). For strict SLA flows, query region-directly or accept fallback to a pinned model.

5) Routing API and scoring model (how decisions are made)
- API: /v1/route-candidates {model, required_gpu_family, min_mem_gb, max_latency_ms, routing_policy}
- Response: list of candidate nodes (node_id) each with: region, gpu_model, health_score, available_concurrency, latency_estimate_ms, reason_tags[] and a score_vector string that contains component scores (latency_score, gpu_match_score, capacity_score, recent_error_penalty).
- Example lightweight scoring formula (configurable per customer): final_score = w_lat*latency_score + w_gpu*gpu_match + w_cap*capacity_score - penalty_errors. Default weights: w_lat=0.5, w_gpu=0.3, w_cap=0.2.
- Important: allow caller to request the score_vector so the client can apply custom policy or audit decisions. We avoid returning only a single opaque winner.

6) Fallbacks and graceful degradation policy:
- If no healthy nodes in preferred region, expand search radius to sister regions (policy: same continent -> global). Each expansion reduces base_score by region_penalty (configurable).
- Maintain short-lived cached fallback mappings in the gateway (TTL 10s) to avoid thundering when a region flaps.
- If GPU matching fails but CPU/batch nodes available, optionally return them with explicit reason_tag: "fallback-cpu". Calling services must opt into CPU fallback.

7) Observability and telemetry (what to emit and how):
- Emit node-level metrics every 30s: health_score, gpu_util_pct_1m, free_mem_mb, concurrent_requests, avg_latency_ms.
- Emit events on state transitions: HEALTHY->DEGRADED, DEGRADED->UNHEALTHY, REGISTERED, DEREGISTERED, GPU_MODEL_CHANGE.
- Tag metrics with region, zone, gpu_model, node_role. Keep tag cardinality low (avoid customer ids as tags; put them in labels[] if needed).
- Flow traces for routing decisions: sample 1-2% of requests to include the routing request -> selected_node trace, store in Jaeger/AWS X-Ray for 7d in dev, 30d in prod (configurable).

8) Operational playbook highlights (short checklist for SREs):
- On region-wide heartbeat loss: check region-registry leader, cross-check message backlog, increase replication rate, run "replay-log" tool.
- On sudden mass GPU errors: rollback recent kernel/driver changes via canary and mark nodes with "driver_probe_failure" tag.
- When performing maintenance that changes GPU labels: set node to maintenance=true before changing gpu_model; agent will emit MODEL_CHANGE event and control plane will gracefully drain.

9) Migration and rollout plan (pragmatic):
- Phase 0: deploy agent and region registry in dev, collect labels and telemetry. No routing changes.
- Phase 1: enable routing API to return score_vector but keep existing router in control (observe only).
- Phase 2: enable soft routing (weighted canary) for internal teams (10% traffic) with emergency kill switch.
- Phase 3: global rollout and policy tuning based on observed false positives (misrouted requests) and health flapping metrics.

10) Open questions / decisions to pick quickly:
- Catalog maintenance: who owns canonical gpu_model list? (Ops + Applied ML?) Suggest productizing a tiny web UI for additions with review workflow.
- Staleness windows: should cross-region staleness be 30s or 60s by default? Leaning 60s to reduce replication cost but need to measure impact on tail latency routing decisions.
- Score explainability: how verbose should score_vector be in customer-visible logs? Privacy/PCI concerns if we include some labels.

Appendix: small checklist for label additions (internal):
- Always add new gpu_model to central catalog with example naming and aliases.
- When adding new node_role, communicate to all router consumers and update documentation.
- Keep label keys to max length 24 chars and values to 48 chars to avoid DB index bloat.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Prototype a minimal region-registry service that accepts agent heartbeats and exposes /v1/nodes?filter=... with simple scoring in Go.
- Wire OpenTelemetry exporter and run in staging for 2 weeks to validate health_score thresholds.
- Draft a small README and quick Confluence page (CONFS-4312) to call out invariants for different teams.

End of note.

(Informal: this doc intentionally mixes architecture and ops heuristics — meant as a reference for engineering + SRE pairing during the next sprint.)
